summary_en: This case checks that calculate_surface_heat evaluates absorbed heat and surface emission for each surface according to equation T4. The parameters are assembled by assemble_thermal_parameters and include the surfaces of the Section 4.4 example, the solar array with its front and back recorded separately, and the radiator with two coating regions. The environments are generated by prepare_surface_environment. The Section 4.4 example, the direct-only environment and the environment with direct sunlight, albedo and infrared together are each evaluated in four orientations: facing the Sun, inclined to the Sun at 60°, edge-on to the Sun at 90° and facing away from the Sun. The albedo-only and infrared-only environments are each evaluated facing the Sun and inclined at 60°, and the environment without external irradiation is evaluated facing the Sun. Component temperatures are 200 K, 300 K and 400 K. Directly constructed environments are also used to check, surface by surface, the effect of the incidence cosine, the absorptivity and the emissivity. In total 470 output values from 94 calls are compared with an independent hand calculation, carried out from the design formulas in decimal arithmetic with 40 significant digits. The maximum relative error is 1.9×10^{−16} against an acceptance limit of 1×10^{−12}. In the Section 4.4 example the absorbed power is 1600 W facing the Sun and 800 W inclined at 60°, and the direct absorbed heat is 0 W both edge-on at 90° and facing away from the Sun. For the solar array and the radiator the ratio of emitted power at 400 K to that at 200 K is 16 in every case, with a maximum relative deviation from 16 of 0. Facing away from the Sun, the direct absorbed heat of the solar array, 1102.41 W, comes entirely from the back side. absorbed_solar_S_W is 0 W in the albedo-only and infrared-only environments and when only the radiator receives direct sunlight. All 18 abnormal inputs give a defined outcome: a temperature that is zero, negative or non-finite, a negative irradiance, or a mismatched run identifier or time raises ThermalInputError naming the field, and repeated calls return identical results. When the solar array at 200 K is below its applicable temperature range of 233.15 K to 373.15 K and the radiator at 400 K is above its applicable temperature range of 173.15 K to 353.15 K, range_warnings lists the corresponding nodes and a ThermalRangeWarning is issued, while absorption and emission are still computed with constant optical properties. The state, environment and parameters are unchanged after the call.
